Header: Mycosphaerella ( syn. Cercospora ) arachidicola , Mycosphaerella berkeleyi ( syn. Cercospora personata )

Prevention: Use disinfected equipment, by using fire or jik/bleach
Avoid mechanical damage to plant stems and roots as fungus can enter plants through wounds
Intercrop with other crops, such as 5 rows of groundnuts with 2 rows of maize.
Use resistant/tolerant varieties, but most are only partially resistant (Bafia, A65, ICGM281, and others).
ICGV 91225 is only tolerant to early leaf spot.
Practise rotation with a non- leguminous crop, e.g. with maize
Monitoring: Regularly visit the field to observe the progress of the plant health.
Look for leaves that show premature defoliation and death.
Early leaf spots have relatively large brown spots, often with a halo
In contrast late leaf spots are small, black spots.
Rust spots are numerous, tiny, powdery and rust brown .
If the above typical symptoms appear on leaves of about 2 to 5 plants out of 20 plants, action may be considered
Direct Control: Uproot the affected plants and use as animal feed.
Infected plants should be used as animal feeds.
Chlorothalonil –based products (Agrothalonil 720SC, Asconil 720SC, Fangonil 50SC, Gilder 720SC, and others).
These belong to the multi-side action group of fungicides.
Restrictions: Wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.

Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (MAFC / TPRI).
U, unlikely hazardous when used as per product instructions.
Pre-harvest interval (p.h.i.) 7 days; restricted re-entry interval (r.e.i.) 1 day after spray.
Max 2 sprays per season after the emergence of the infection, at intervals of 10 - 15 days starting 40 days after germination up to 90 days.
This provides effective control to early and late leaf spots.
Do not use near water sources.
